_about: Kirsopp Lake’s footnotes to his Greek and Latin text (ℵ Codex Sinaiticus; A the Athos manuscript; H the Hamburg fragment; Pam the Amherst papyrus; Pox Oxyrhynchus papyri; L1 the Vulgate Latin, L2 the Palatine Latin, L both; E the Ethiopic; C the Sahidic; Clem. Clement of Alexandria; Athan. pseudo-Athanasius; Ant. Antiochus of Palestine), and in "refs" the passages of Scripture he prints in the margin (with the digital file’s own reference, "urn"). The digital file has only the text pages, so the footnotes Lake prints under his English translation on the facing pages are not here. "at" is the verse the note or reference stands in ("c:0": the heading above the division that begins at chapter c). Greek inside a note is in Beta Code, as in the digital file (so h(mw=n = ἡμῶν; "#3" is q), and the file has slips in the notes’ English ("shich" = which, "folloss" = follows); those checked against Lake’s printed page are corrected, with the evidence in "fixed". From First1KGreek (Open Greek and Latin), CC BY-SA 4.0.

At this point A ends, as the last leaf is missing. The Latin text shich folloss is that of L1. The fes verses in Greek are from Pam. Some sords have been restored as the Papyrus is in bad condition, but the reconstructions are almost certain.
The Greek shich folloss is a #3uotation preserved in Antiochus.
